body:
- **Reverse DCF / expectations investing (Mauboussin & Rappaport).**
  - The method starts from the current price and solves for the expectations it implies (price-implied expectations, or PIE). It does not forecast and discount. — [Motley Fool Q&A with Mauboussin & Rappaport](https://www.fool.com/investing/2022/01/19/expectations-investing-qanda-mauboussin-rappaport); [Mauboussin book excerpt PDF](https://www.michaelmauboussin.com/s/EIexcerpt.pdf)
  - The value drivers are revenue growth, operating (NOPBT) margin and investment rate. The value determinants are cash tax rate, WACC and the market-implied forecast period (the market-implied competitive advantage period, MICAP). — [CFA Path summary](https://cfapath.substack.com/p/expectations-investing); [Cowboy Computer review](https://cowboycomputer.substack.com/p/book-review-expectations-investing)
  - The process has three steps: (1) estimate PIE; (2) identify the "expectations opportunities" by finding the value trigger (sales, costs or investment) with the biggest impact; (3) buy or sell when your view differs from PIE.
  - A free reverse DCF spreadsheet is on the companion site. A DCF can understate the value of optionality, so the authors suggest adding real-options analysis for highly uncertain firms. — [Motley Fool AU](https://www.fool.com.au/2022/01/20/expectations-investing-a-qampa-with-michael-mauboussin-and-alfred-rappaport-usfeed/)
- **Twin or double engine.** Total return ≈ (1+EPS growth) × (1+change in P/E) × … + dividend yield. 100-baggers need both EPS growth and multiple expansion. — [Validea on Mayer](https://blog.validea.com/?p=33794); [Hedge Fund Alpha on Motilal 100x](https://hedgefundalpha.com/strategies/100x-power-growth-wealth-creation/)
- **PEG.** PEG = P/E ÷ EPS growth rate (%). Lynch treats 1 as fair value; practitioners treat <1 as cheap and >1.5–2 as expensive. — [Value Research](https://www.valueresearchonline.com/stories/51021/peter-lynch-s-six-stock-categories/)
- **ROCE at Fundsmith.** Holdings typically earn 25–30%. — [Trustnet](https://www.trustnet.com/news/662915/three-simple-steps-to-making-returns-like-terry-smith)
- **Marcellus thresholds.** ROCE >15% and revenue growth >10% in every year for 10 years. — [Marcellus newsletter](https://marcellus.in/newsletter/consistent-compounders/valuing-longevity-of-healthy-fundamentals/)
- **Owner earnings formula.** See section 1. — [1986 Berkshire letter](https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1986.html)
- **Graham thresholds.** P/E ≤15, P/B ≤1.5, P/E×P/B ≤22.5, current ratio ≥2. See section 1. [primary, not re-fetched]

**Standard formula reference.** These are textbook definitions, for example from Damodaran's [Investment Valuation resources at NYU Stern](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/). The thresholds are common practitioner conventions and are not tied to one source unless noted. [not re-fetched]

body:
- **For a retail checklist.** A combination of profitability (ROCE/ROIC, gross profit/assets), safety (low leverage, low volatility, stable earnings) and value (FCF yield, EV/EBITDA) is the academically defensible core. Of these, profitability and safety are most aligned with what Buffett did.
- **Small caps.** "Size matters if you control your junk" supports the small-cap tilt in Indian frameworks (SQGLP's "S", SMILE's "Small") *only when combined with a quality filter*. Small caps without a quality screen historically underperform.
- **India.** Indian factor evidence exists but was not researched here (e.g. IIM Ahmedabad's Indian Fama-French factor data library and NSE's Nifty quality/value indices). The authors of the US papers report international robustness for QMJ (24 countries), but specific Indian results were not verified.

`insight:india-mb-pe70-exit` · confidence: verified

Fifteen winners reached trailing P/E ≥70 at the end of their up-move: Bajaj Finance 121 (2021), Astral 118, Pidilite 93, Deepak 93, Dixon 197, Tata Elxsi 103, KPIT 86, Trent 232, Cochin 95, Kaynes 203, CDSL 76, Symphony 84, Page 81, La Opala 70, Alkyl 76. Price change from that peak to 19 Nov 2026: Symphony −74%, KPIT −72%, Tata Elxsi −64%, Alkyl −64%, Kaynes −62%, Cochin −60%, Astral −48%, La Opala −48%, Deepak −46%, Page −42%, Trent −41%, Dixon −29%, CDSL −27%, Pidilite +28%, Bajaj Finance +39%. Median −48%; 13 of 15 negative. The two positive cases still underperformed their own EPS growth, which was 2x and 4.8x. Winners that peaked at 40–60x (Eicher 51, Balkrishna 49, HAL 49, Mazagon 52, Polycab 59, Garware 42, Avanti 45, Caplin 69) did better, with a median of about −25% and several recovering to new highs. The trigger was almost always P/E ≥70 combined with decelerating EPS (Page FY23, Astral FY22–26, Elxsi FY26, Trent LFL, Alkyl spreads, KPIT Europe). Rule for memory: P/E ≥70 alone is not a sell signal (Trent 2020 at 155 worked because EPS was depressed), but P/E ≥70 with the first quarter of EPS deceleration has a poor base rate. Trim rather than hope.

`case_study:trent-2020-2024` · tickers: TRENT · confidence: verified

₹294 (May 2020) → ATH ₹5,490 (Oct 2024) ≈19x (≈310x from the 2008 low ₹17.7). Trailing P/E 155 → 232 (only 1.5x), so implied EPS rose ~12.5x and the move was earnings-driven even though the starting P/E looked absurd: COVID had depressed EPS. Revenue FY21 ₹2,593 cr → FY26 ₹20,074 cr; OPM 4% → 19%; ROCE 1% → ~31%. Drawdown inside the run only −22%; −43% in COVID (Feb–May 2020). Early signal: Zudio, a low-price fashion format, was opening hundreds of stores with fast paybacks. Store adds and like-for-like (LFL) growth were disclosed in quarterly updates, and Westside margins held. An alert investor could have read the unit economics rather than the trailing P/E. Ended/stalled: LFL growth slowed from double digits to low single digits or negative in FY26, newer Tier-2 stores had lower sales throughput, and there were repeated sell-offs on business updates (Apr, Jul, Oct, Nov 2025; −10% in Jul 2026). The stock fell −59% to ₹2,266 (Mar 2026) and is ₹3,225 on 19 Nov 2026 (P/E ~90). Lesson: a high trailing P/E is not disqualifying when earnings are cyclically depressed and unit economics are visible. In retail, LFL deceleration is the exit signal.

Key data: **start_year**: 2020; **end_year**: 2024; **start_price**: 294; **end_price**: 5490; **price_nov2026**: 3225; **multiple**: ~19x (310x from 2008); **pe_start**: 154.6; **pe_end**: 231.5; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~12.5x; **max_drawdown**: -22% in run; -59% after; **early_signals**: Zudio store adds + paybacks in quarterly updates; **ended**: LFL slowdown FY26; **lesson**: watch LFL, not trailing P/E

Sources: <https://www.screener.in/company/TRENT/consolidated/> · <https://www.outlookbusiness.com/amp/story/markets/trent-shares-slump-4-as-revenue-growth-falters-in-q4> · <https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/trent-stock-falls-growth-slowdown-valuation-pressures-q1fy26-125070401184_1.html> · <https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/trent-shares-fall-10-as-q1-biz-update-disappoints-heres-why-541322-2026-07-07> · <https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/trent-slides-6pc-to-lowest-since-june-2024-on-weak-demand-after-soft-q2-125111000181_1.html>

`insight:marks-private-credit-fiscal-2026` | confidence: single-source | date: 2026-09-22

Apr-2026 memo (published 9 Apr 2026): private equity returns have 'fallen precipitously' (MSCI estimate cited: US PE funds ~5.8% annualised 2022-Q3 2025 vs 11.6% for the S&P 500); future private-loan performance depends on sponsor skill and on exits; weak borrowers increasingly use payment-in-kind (PIK) interest instead of cash service. Lenders' security comes from borrower performance and seniority; disciplined underwriters will be fine. Marks closes by quoting Oaktree's Bob O'Leary comparing today to the high-yield bust of 1989-91: a new instrument over-indulged, then spooked by a Middle East war - 'Ultimately, high yield was fine (even great), and direct lending will be as well, but it may have to go through a credit cycle to get to a better place.' Sep-2026 'Part III' memo: 'you can't ignore the laws of economics and expect to come out ahead'; the US cannot 'perpetually spend more than it takes in' without its 'currency and Treasury securities' being 'disrespected'; but selling US stocks is not the answer since dollar cash and bonds carry the same risk, and non-US assets bring 'other risks' (slower growth, regulation, EM uncertainty). Modest diversification makes sense for 'investors with non-dollar needs.' Actionable for an Indian investor: rising PIK share is a stress signal in any credit book (including Indian NBFC/AIF credit); US fiscal risk argues for INR-based core holdings with only considered USD diversification.

Sources:
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/insights/memo/whats-going-on-in-private-credit
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/insights/memo/shall-we-repeal-the-laws-of-economics---part-iii

Two plain Python 3 scripts (standard library only, plus the system `curl` for BSE) that run
unattended on a Raspberry Pi, collect Indian exchange disclosures every evening and flag changes
worth a human look. No Claude, no pip packages, no API keys.

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| `collect.py` | Pulls NSE corporate announcements (main board + SME), PIT insider disclosures, SAST Reg 29, bulk and block deals, the all-company NSE promoter-pledge snapshot, and BSE announcements as a backup feed. Raw responses are kept gzipped under `$FEIN_DATA/raw/YYYY-MM-DD/`; normalised rows go into `$FEIN_DATA/fein.sqlite`. |
| `detect.py` | Runs the rules below over the database and writes `$FEIN_DATA/alerts/YYYY-MM-DD.md` and `.csv` (columns: date, symbol, rule, details, source_url). An alert is reported once, on the day it is first seen. |
| `fein_common.py` | Shared code: HTTP with pacing and back-off, date/number parsing, SQLite schema. |

`FEIN_DATA` defaults to `~/fein-data`. Logs go to `$FEIN_DATA/logs/collect.log` and `detect.log`.

This is a research tool, not SEBI-registered advice. An alert means "open the filing", not "trade".
